title: Throughput safepoints and graded KV throttling to stabilize micro-batching under high QPS
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem statement:
Under sustained high QPS we observe oscillations in micro-batch sizing and KV cache churn that cause P95 latency spikes and elevated GPU memory pressure. Existing admission logic is binary (admit or reject based on a fixed threshold) which leads to synchronized bursts and repeated KV eviction thrashing.

Goals:
- Smooth micro-batch sizing so per-request tail latency and error rates remain within SLOs during spikes.
- Reduce unnecessary KV cache evictions and GPU memory oversubscription by introducing graded backpressure and safepoints where batching decisions are re-evaluated.
- Keep throughput high for priority traffic while gracefully degrading lower-priority requests.

Proposed solution summary:
1) Throughput safepoints: periodic evaluation points (safepoints) where the scheduler recomputes target microbatch sizes using a short-term predictor (10s EWMA + surge detector). Safepoints decouple admission decisions from per-request timing jitter and reduce synchronized resizing.
2) Graded KV throttling: instead of immediate eviction or full rejection, requests are placed into priority tiers. Lower tiers are subject to incremental delays (ms backoffs), optional soft-prefetch deferral, and selective no-evict hints; higher tiers bypass soft-throttle. Throttles are expressed as a graded multiplier on the microbatch admission window.
3) GPU memory-aware reclaim policy: introduce small proactive compaction windows at safepoints where cold KV slabs (based on hotness TTL) are asynchronously compacted or offloaded to host pinned memory before eviction. This reduces large eviction spikes.
4) Admission controller enhancements: combine request priority, observed prefix-KV-hit-rate, and headroom estimate to compute a composite admission score. The headroom estimator uses short-term GPU mem util + inflight microbatch footprint to predict near-future pressure.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs stability: safepoints add global coordination latency but reduce oscillation; tuned to a 100-500ms cadence.
- Extra CPU/host memory for pinned offload reduces eviction frequency but increases cost.
- Graded throttling increases median latency slightly for low-priority traffic but reduces tail and error rate for all.

Link artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Safepoints+and+Graded+KV+Throttling
- Spike notebook and simulator: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-spike-sim
- Initial PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1314
- Canary dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rv9h-safepoints/canary-batching

Acceptance criteria:
- P95 latency on canary region does not regress by more than 5% compared to baseline under a 2x synthetic QPS spike for 5 minutes.
- Tail error rate (5xx and OOMs) reduces by >=50% in the canary window versus baseline spike tests.
- KV eviction rate (evictions/sec) reduced by >=30% during sustained high QPS in synthetic tests.
- No increase in cost beyond expected host-memory offload baseline (monitor offload bytes/sec).
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency regression <= 5% during 2x QPS spike (5m)
Tail 5xx/OOMs reduced by >= 50% in canary tests
KV evictions/sec reduced by >= 30% during sustained high QPS
Observable offload bandwidth within expected budget
testing_plan: Unit tests for safepoint scheduler and graded-throttle state machine
Offline simulation with synthetic QPS bursts and realistic prefix distributions (use spike notebook)
Hardware-in-loop canary on non-critical region (10% of pods) with progressive ramping to 100% of canary pool
Chaos test: inject KV slab eviction delays and host-offload failures to validate graceful fallback
A/B experiment comparing current admission vs safepoints over 48h window
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated implementation (runtime.safepoints.enabled = false by default)
Canary: enable for 5% of production capacity for 24h, monitored by SRE
Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 days if metrics meet acceptance criteria
Fallback path: runtime.safepoints.enabled=false AND runtime.admission.fallback_mode=legacy to roll back quickly
Post-rollout: run 2-week observation, evaluate cost and cache stability metrics
notes: We will reuse the headroom estimator developed in ENG-61207 with a short-time constant for surge sensitivity
This design favors reducing tail and errors over minimizing median latency for background traffic
Need coordination with infra billing to track any host-memory offload cost impact
